title: Run a command on piped input using xargs
summary: Use xargs to pass the output of one command as arguments to another. This is useful when a command doesn't accept piped input directly, like passing a list of files to `rm` or `echo`.

steps.explain: Pipe the output of a source command into xargs, followed by the command you want to run. xargs splits the input into arguments.

placeholders.name: ARGUMENTS_SOURCE
placeholders.description: The command whose output will be used as arguments (e.g., 'ls', 'find . -name *.txt')

placeholders.name: COMMAND
placeholders.description: The command to execute with those arguments (e.g., 'echo', 'rm')
